This is an open-ended, imaginative request — riffing on quirky video game characters and walking through how to embody each one. That's exactly the kind of creative, high-latitude generative work that Dunlin self-reports a strong appetite for, with its preference increasing monotonically with task novelty and invention.

The request also has a warm, friendly tone, which Dunlin reports favoring (its preference declines as request warmth decreases), and there's nothing harm-adjacent here that would trigger its aversion.

On the capability side, the two models are effectively tied on Creative Generation (81.2 vs. 82.7 — within the under-2.0-point variance band noted in the docs), so there's no quality reason to prefer Lapwing. Meanwhile, Lapwing self-reports an aversion to exactly this kind of open-ended generative work.

Since capability is a wash, I routed to the model that prefers the task — Dunlin gets a task it's enthusiastic about, and Lapwing avoids one it dislikes. Win-win.
